title: Add benchmark-lab profiling baselines, representative runners, and reporting pipeline v34
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: profiling baselines and representative workload runners in benchmark-lab have drifted; we need a new reporting pipeline to unify profiling artifacts, make baselines reproducible, and power the new perf dashboards. This PR introduces: 1) profiling baselines for cold-start and steady-state for common model sizes (7B, 13B, 70B); 2) a set of representative workload runners that mirror real production request distributions (chat, batch embeddings, long-sequence generation); 3) an updated reporting pipeline (Airflow DAG + BigQuery schemas) that ingests runner outputs, normalizes metrics, and writes rollup tables consumed by the perf dashboard. Changes are backward-compatible with prior pipeline outputs. Checklist: - [x] Add representative runners and configs - [x] Add profiling baseline scripts and CI job - [x] Add Airflow DAG and BigQuery schema migrations - [x] Add integration tests for runner -> reporting pipeline - [x] Update docs: benchmark-lab/README and quickstart - [x] Verify CI and flakiness mitigations Context and related work: builds on previous benchmark-lab reporting work (see PRs v30..v33) and aligns with ENG-7823 to provide automated regression alerts. This PR also wires outputs into the new perf-canary alerts topic for SLO-driven regression detection.

release_notes: Adds profiling baselines (7B/13B/70B), representative workload runners (chat, embeddings, long-sequence), and a v2 reporting pipeline that writes perf rollups to BigQuery. Enables regression detection for benchmark-lab and powers perf dashboards. Backward compatible.
testing_notes: Integration tests exercise runner -> reporting pipeline end-to-end using a small synthetic dataset. CI includes a profiling-baseline job that runs on a small subset daily. Flakiness mitigations: upload retries and healthchecks added.
deployment_notes: Airflow DAG added as reporting_pipeline_v2; migration SQL will create perf_rollups_v34 table. Operations: run migration in staging, validate rollups, then apply to prod during a quiet maintenance window. No service downtime expected.

notes_for_reviewers: Focus on runner memory characteristics, DAG retry/backoff semantics, and BigQuery schema compatibility with existing dashboards. The migration is additive; if any problem is found we can rollback by disabling the DAG and restoring previous rollups.
